summary: Defines the Link-Template HTTP header field, which describes the structure of a link between resources so that clients can generate new links from it. It is a template-based counterpart to the Link header field.

eli5.summary: Instead of listing every address, a web server can hand you a fill-in-the-blanks pattern. You put in your own words and get the right address.

questions: how to describe url templates in http headers
how does link-template differ from link header
how do uri templates work in http headers
subtitle: An HTTP header that carries link templates, so clients can build links by filling in variables.

tldr.problem: The Link header field carries links directly, but there is no standard way to describe a link whose target depends on variables that the client fills in.
tldr.mechanism: The Link-Template header field is a Structured Field List of Strings, each holding a URI Template plus Parameters such as rel, anchor and var-base.
tldr.outcome: Clients can expand the templates to generate new links. The field is registered as permanent in the HTTP Field Name Registry.

today: RFC 9652 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Templates for Links
sections.content: RFC 6570 defines URI Templates, which turn into a URI when expanded with a set of variables. This RFC defines an HTTP header field that carries such templates in message headers. It is complementary to the Link header field of RFC 8288, which carries links directly.
sections.eli5: Rather than handing out one address, the server hands out an address with blanks you can fill in.

sections.title: The Link-Template Field
sections.content:
Link-Template is a Structured Field (RFC 9651) whose value is a List of Strings. Each String holds a URI Template and can have Parameters carrying metadata. It is semantically equivalent to the Link header field, except that the link target and link anchor can contain URI Templates. The target is found by expanding the template and converting it to an absolute URI if necessary.

The link context and relation type are given by the anchor and rel Parameters, whose values MUST be Strings. Only anchor MAY contain a URI Template. Other target attributes are Parameters whose values MUST be Strings, or Display Strings when they contain non-ASCII characters. Implementations MUST support all levels of template defined by RFC 6570 in the link String and the anchor Parameter.

For example, Link-Template: "/{username}"; rel="item" says a resource with relation type "item" for a given "username" can be found by expanding the "username" variable.
sections.eli5: Each entry is a pattern like a street name with a blank for the house number, plus little notes saying what kind of link it is.

sections.title: The var-base Parameter
sections.content:
A templated link can carry a var-base Parameter whose value is a URI-reference used as a base URI for the variable names in the template. This lets variables be globally identified instead of being specific to the context of use. Dereferencing a variable's URI might lead to more information about it, but the format of that information is out of scope.

The variable URI is found by resolving the name against the var-base value as in RFC 3986. If the result is still relative, the link's context is used as the base in a further resolution. With var-base="https://example.org/vars/", the variable widget_id is identified as https://example.org/vars/widget_id.
sections.eli5: It gives each blank a full, unique name, so everyone agrees what the blank means.

sections.title: Security and Registration
sections.content:
The security considerations of the Link header field and of URI Templates apply. Target attributes sent as Display Strings can be vulnerable to a wide variety of attacks, and the RFC points to Unicode security guidance without giving specific advice.

The field name Link-Template is entered into the HTTP Field Name Registry with status Permanent.
sections.eli5: Names with unusual letters can be used for tricks, so programs should handle them carefully.
